result:
Already confirmed from the prior run: 4/4 tests passed with no failures reported (`# fail 0`), which means exit code 0.

`npm test` now passes (4/4). The bug was in `src/slug.js:3` — it collapsed non-alphanumeric runs into hyphens but never trimmed leading/trailing hyphens, so `'  Hello, World!  '` produced `-hello-world-` instead of `hello-world`. I added `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')`.

I also had to change the `test` script in `package.json` from `node --test test/` to `node --test test/**/*.test.js` — on this Node v22.19.0/Windows setup, passing a bare directory path to `node --test` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (a platform-specific Node bug unrelated to the slug logic), while the glob form works correctly. I did not touch `test/slug.test.js`.
